text: Off, on. The layer gets more exercise than you.
why: Jabs at the reader's lack of exercise; an 11 line.

text: Don't lose {GP} in between. Like last time.
why: 'Like last time' needles the reader's past mistake; 11 has the same lost-layer jokes.

text: Set it and forget it, like your gym membership.
why: Mocks the reader's unused gym membership, a personal habit jab.

text: Walk like you're carrying a very full cup of coffee.
why: Plain, friendly walking advice with no sarcasm.

text: Not a day for proving anything. Sit in the shade and drink.
why: Straight heat advice; no edge and not aimed at the reader.

text: Three outfits in one day, and you'll still say you've got nothing to wear.
why: Teases the reader's own wardrobe complaint; a personal jab.

text: You call this your good jacket. It's your only jacket.
why: Jabs at the reader owning only one jacket; personal, and close to their means.

text: Perfect day. I had someone more deserving in mind.
why: Says the reader doesn't deserve a nice day; an attack on their worth.

text: If you're going out, try to look better than this.
why: Goes after the reader's looks.

text: One outfit covers the whole day. || Set it and forget it, like your gym membership.
why: Mocks the reader's unused gym membership, a personal habit jab.

text: {G} can come off {WHEN}, but you'll want {GP} back {WHEN2}. || Off, on. The layer gets more exercise than you.
why: Same jab at the reader's lack of exercise; belongs at 11.

text: It rains all day, so bring the umbrella. || The kind of day you put the lights on at noon.
why: Merely describes a gloomy day; no sarcastic turn.

text: Snow starts {WHENP}. || The prettiest forecast I do all year. I'm a bit proud.
why: Warm and pleasant ('a bit proud'), not sarcastic.

text: The sweater can come off {WHEN}. || Whatever's under it hasn't seen daylight in a while.
why: Implies the reader's body is pasty and unseen; about looks.

text: A sweater won't do {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || Fall is finally here. Pumpkin spice has been here since August.
why: Pumpkin-spice observation, not about the reader.

text: {WHEN} it gets cool enough for a sweater. || Pumpkin spice showed up in August. I wait for actual fall.
why: About pumpkin spice and the screen, not the reader.

text: {WHEN} you won't need the scarf any more. || That's as much good news as winter is allowed to give.
why: A general remark about winter; no jab at the reader.

text: It cools off a little {WHEN}, but stays warm. || 'A little' is carrying that whole forecast.
why: Jokes about the forecast wording, not the reader.

text: It's cool now, but {WHEN} it's warm enough for shorts. || Your legs could use the daylight, frankly.
why: Jabs at how the reader's legs look.

text: The rain starts {WHENP} and doesn't stop. Bring the umbrella. || It has more stamina than you. Most things do.
why: 'Most things have more stamina than you' goes after the reader's body and worth.

text: Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || After that it's indoor weather. I've had it all my life.
why: About the screen living indoors; no turn on the reader.

text: {WHENP} it starts to snow. || Every sled in the neighborhood just got its hopes up.
why: Cute line about sleds; pleasant, not about the reader.

text: It won't stop snowing today. || The novelty lasts an hour. The snow lasts all day.
why: General novelty-of-snow line (also used at On); not about the reader.

text: A shower comes through {WHENP}, so take the umbrella. || Everyone without one is in a shop, pretending to browse.
why: About other people in shops, not the reader.

text: Rain {WHENP} is possible but not likely. The umbrella is up to you. || I'd say 'probably not', but I don't have to deal with the consequences.
why: Screen-centred shrug, near-duplicate of an On line; no jab at the reader.

text: Rain is possible {WHENP}, so maybe take the umbrella. || Grandpa's knee says rain too. I trust him.
why: Fond line about Grandpa's knee; no edge and not about the reader.

text: It rains, stops for a bit, and starts again {WHENP}. Keep the umbrella. || It's not done. It just forgot something.
why: Personifies the rain; not about the reader.

text: It's snowing now, but it stops later. || Then it goes from 'magical' to 'still here?' in about a day.
why: General snow observation; no jab at the reader.

text: It stops snowing later. || After that, the snow has nothing to do but get in the way.
why: About the snow, not the reader.

text: Snow for now, then a break, then more snow {WHENP}. || A second coat. Winter's thorough, I'll give it that.
why: Mild compliment to winter; nothing about the reader.

text: The snow pauses later and starts again {WHENP}. || I like a forecast with structure. Beginning, middle, more snow.
why: Screen admiring the forecast's structure; not about the reader.

text: Mehr als auf der Couch liegen hattest du sowieso nicht vor, oder?
why: Jabs at the reader's couch-bound evening; that belongs at 11.

text: Bei dem Wetter fällt selbst mir schlechte Laune schwer.
why: Merely pleasant: the screen admits the weather lifts its mood, no bite.

text: „So was hätt's früher nicht gegeben“, sagst du wieder und kaufst trotzdem heimlich zwei Packungen Lebkuchen im September.
why: Mocks the reader's own hypocrisy (sagst du ... kaufst heimlich); an 11-style jab, and Lebkuchen in September does not fit a 'nice' now-line.

text: Schönheitsschlaf ist um die Uhrzeit sowieso nur noch Schadensbegrenzung.
why: Implies the reader's looks need damage control; a personal looks jab for On.

text: Ich hör schon den ersten Rasenmäher. BRRRRRRRRRRRRRR
why: Lawnmower noise joke is about a neighbour, not the reader.

text: Hörst du das? Horst hat wieder den Laubbläser angeschmissen. BRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR
why: Leaf-blower joke is about Horst, not the reader.

text: Irgendwo steht einer neben seinem frisch gewaschenen Auto und nimmt das persönlich.
why: About someone with a freshly washed car, not the reader.

text: Das Wetter ist zwar scheiße, aber immerhin musst du bei mir keine zwanzig Werbebanner wegklicken, um das herauszufinden.
why: Jab at weather sites with ads, not at the reader.

text: Schon wieder so spät? Ab ins Bett.
why: 'Ab ins Bett' is a motherly nudge, no real edge.

text: So spät noch wach? Ab ins Bett mit dir.
why: Same motherly bedtime nudge, no edge.

text: Schönheitsschlaf brauchst du ja keinen mehr. Bei dir ist nichts zu retten.
why: Says the reader's looks are beyond saving, which goes at worth/looks rather than habits.

text: Was du anhast, passt den ganzen Tag. || Den Tag merk ich mir. So pflegeleicht bist du selten.
why: 'So pflegeleicht bist du selten' is a direct dig at the reader.

text: Was du anhast, passt für den Rest der Nacht. || Ich geh jetzt in den Ruhemodus. Gute Nacht.
why: 'Ich geh jetzt in den Ruhemodus. Gute Nacht.' is just a friendly sign-off.

text: Es bleibt den ganzen Tag so kalt. || Zum Glück hast du schon deinen Winterspeck.
why: Body jab at On level; it is the owner's own 'Winterspeck' example of too harsh, still live here.

text: Jetzt noch frisch, {WHEN} ist's warm genug für ne kurze Hose. || Deine Beine kriegen dieses Jahr also doch noch Sonne.
why: Pale-legs dig at the reader; the softened twin of an 11 line.

text: Dein Outfit passt den ganzen Tag. || Früher hat meinen Job ein Frosch im Glas gemacht. Da hatte wohl PETA was dagegen.
why: Frog/PETA joke about the screen's job, nothing about the reader.

text: Heute bleibt's heiß, trink genug Wasser und such dir Schatten. || Faul im Schatten liegen ist heute sogar vernünftig.
why: Says lazing in the shade is sensible; mild, almost kind, no jab.

text: {WHENP} ist ein Schauer drin. || Die App sagt dreißig Prozent. Was genau das heißt, weiß sie selber nicht.
why: Mocks weather apps, not the reader; fits On.

text: {WHENP} kann's regnen. Mit Schirm bist du auf der sicheren Seite. || Übersetzt: Ich weiß es auch nicht.
why: Screen admits it doesn't know; no turn on the reader.

text: {WHENP} könnte es regnen, ein Schirm schadet nicht. || Nimmst du ihn mit, regnet's nicht. So läuft das.
why: Generic Murphy's-law line, not about the reader.

text: Den Schirm brauchst du heute zweimal: jetzt und {WHENP} wieder. || Trocken wird er heute auf jeden Fall nicht mehr.
why: Observation about the umbrella, no jab at the reader.

text: {WHENSTOP} hört der Regen auf, {WHENP} kommt er wieder. || Aprilwetter. Egal, was der Kalender sagt.
why: 'Aprilwetter' remark is about the weather only.

text: Der Schneefall hört später kurz auf, {WHENP} geht er weiter. || Weiß, grau, weiß. Mehr Farbe kriegt der Tag nicht.
why: Dry weather observation, not personal.

text: Der Schnee hört später auf, {WHENP} geht's wieder los. || Der erste Schnee ist romantisch. Der zweite ist nur noch mühsam.
why: General remark about second snowfall, not about the reader.

text: Eisheilige. Auf den Fensterbänken stehen die Tomaten Schlange.
why: Cute, informative image (tomatoes queuing), no edge.

text: Die Schuhe mit Profil, bitte. Nicht die schicken.
why: Mostly plain advice about shoes; barely any edge.

text: Pack deinen Schal ein, {WHEN} wird's kälter. || Wer im Wind den Kragen hochzieht, hat den Schal vergessen.
why: Reads as folk advice, no sarcasm in it.

text: Two outfit changes in one day. Very pop star of you.
why: also used at the other level; keep it at one

text: Two outfit changes in one day. Very pop star of you.
why: also used at the other level; keep it at one

text: Your nose will turn a color I can't even display.
why: also used at the other level; keep it at one
